items.notes: Quelle sounds exactly like quel, so only the feminine noun sauce shows the correct spelling.

items.fr: Bien qu'il soit tard, elle continue à préparer le repas.
items.en: Although it is late, she keeps preparing the meal.
items.ipa: /bjɛ̃ kil swa taʁ ɛl kɔ̃tiny a pʁepaʁe lə ʁəpa/
items.notes: The subjunctive soit ends in a silent t that is easy to drop by mistake.

items.fr: Il faudrait que vous ajoutiez un peu plus de sel.
items.en: You should add a little more salt.
items.ipa: /il fodʁɛ kə vuz‿aʒutje œ̃ pø ply də sɛl/
items.notes: The ending -iez is pronounced yé, which is easy to confuse with the simpler -ez ending.

items.fr: Elle doute que ce dessert soit vraiment sans sucre.
items.en: She doubts this dessert is really sugar free.
items.ipa: /ɛl dut kə sə desɛʁ swa vʁɛmɑ̃ sɑ̃ sykʁ/
items.notes: Sans sounds identical to sang and cent, so only context fixes the spelling.

items.fr: Les invités, bien qu'ils aient déjà mangé, reprennent du gâteau.
items.en: The guests, although they already ate, take more cake.
items.ipa: /lez‿ɛ̃vite bjɛ̃ kilz‿ɛ deʒa mɑ̃ʒe ʁəpʁɛn dy gato/
items.notes: The subjunctive aient is pronounced just like est, with the whole ending staying silent.

items.fr: Ce cuisinier ne se souvient plus de la recette exacte.
items.en: This cook no longer remembers the exact recipe.
items.ipa: /sə kɥizinje nə sə suvjɛ̃ ply də la ʁəsɛt ɛgzakt/
items.notes: Ce and se appear together here and sound completely identical.

items.fr: Mes parents pensent que ces légumes sont meilleurs que les surgelés.
items.en: My parents think these vegetables are better than frozen ones.
items.ipa: /me paʁɑ̃ pɑ̃s kə se legym sɔ̃ mɛjœʁ kə le syʁʒəle/
items.notes: Ces is a homophone of ses and c'est, easily mixed up while writing quickly.

items.fr: Il semble que les enfants aient adoré le repas.
items.en: It seems the children loved the meal.
items.ipa: /il sɑ̃bl kə lez‿ɑ̃fɑ̃z‿ɛ adɔʁe lə ʁəpa/
items.notes: The liaison before aient sounds just like the liaison before ont, so the two are easy to confuse when writing.

items.fr: Je voudrais que tu choisisses un dessert pour ce soir.
items.en: I would like you to choose a dessert for tonight.
items.ipa: /ʒə vudʁɛ kə ty ʃwazis œ̃ desɛʁ puʁ sə swaʁ/
items.notes: The subjunctive choisisses is pronounced exactly like the indicative choisis, with the extra letters staying silent.

items.fr: Nous avons besoin d'un grand chef pour organiser ce banquet.
items.en: We need a great chef to organize this banquet.
items.ipa: /nuz‿avɔ̃ bəzwɛ̃ dœ̃ gʁɑ̃ ʃɛf puʁ ɔʁganize sə bɑ̃kɛ/
items.notes: De un is never said aloud, so it becomes d'un before the vowel.

items.fr: Ce dessert paraît trop sucré pour certains invités.
items.en: This dessert seems too sweet for some guests.
items.ipa: /sə desɛʁ paʁɛ tʁo sykʁe puʁ sɛʁtɛ̃z‿ɛ̃vite/
items.notes: Certains and invités both carry nasal vowels that hide any separate n sound before the liaison.

items.fr: Les grands chefs insistent pour que les ingrédients soient frais.
items.en: Great chefs insist that the ingredients be fresh.
items.ipa: /le gʁɑ̃ ʃɛfz‿ɛ̃sist puʁ kə lez‿ɛ̃gʁedjɑ̃ swat fʁɛ/
items.notes: The liaison after plural chefs is easy to mistake for the sound of a singular chef alone.

items.fr: Elle a l'habitude de goûter chaque plat avant qu'il ne soit servi.
items.en: She usually tastes every dish before it is served.
items.ipa: /ɛl a labityd də gute ʃak pla avɑ̃ kil nə swa sɛʁvi/
items.notes: La habitude cannot be pronounced, so it elides to l'habitude.

items.fr: Ses amis pensent que ce restaurant mérite trois étoiles.
items.en: Her friends think this restaurant deserves three stars.
items.ipa: /sez‿ami pɑ̃s kə sə ʁɛstɔʁɑ̃ meʁit tʁwaz‿etwal/
items.notes: Ses sounds the same as ce and c'est, so only grammar reveals the right spelling.

items.fr: Il vaut mieux que nous réservions une table avant huit heures.
items.en: It is better that we reserve a table before eight o'clock.
items.ipa: /il vo mjø kə nu ʁezɛʁvjɔ̃ yn tabl avɑ̃ ɥit‿œʁ/
items.notes: The t of huit is silent alone but reappears in liaison before the vowel of heures.

items.fr: C'est étonnant que ces enfants aiment autant les épinards.
items.en: It is surprising that these children like spinach so much.
items.notes: C'est and ces are pronounced the same way, distinguishable only by their spelling and role.

items.fr: Quelles épices utilises-tu pour ce curry maison?
items.en: Which spices do you use for this homemade curry?
items.ipa: /kɛlz‿episɛ ytiliz ty puʁ sə kyʁi mɛzɔ̃/
items.notes: Quelles épices links with a z liaison that must still be spelled as two separate words.

items.fr: Bien que ce gâteau soit simple, il plaît à tout le monde.
items.en: Although this cake is simple, everyone likes it.
items.ipa: /bjɛ̃ kə sə gato swa sɛ̃pl il plɛ a tu lə mɔ̃d/
items.notes: Plaît keeps a circumflex accent on the i, a silent spelling detail carried over from plaire.

items.fr: Nous doutons que ses économies suffisent pour ce restaurant étoilé.
items.en: We doubt her savings are enough for this starred restaurant.
items.ipa: /nu dutɔ̃ kə sez‿ekɔnɔmi syfiz puʁ sə ʁɛstɔʁɑ̃ etwale/
items.notes: Ses is a classic homophone trap, sounding identical to ce and c'est.
Sont sounds like son; only the verb context tells you to add the final t.

items.fr: La cuisine est à côté du salon.
items.en: The kitchen is next to the living room.
items.notes: "à" (preposition, with accent) must not be confused with "a" (verb avoir), even though both sound the same.

items.fr: Il y a un grand lit dans la chambre.
items.en: There is a big bed in the bedroom.
items.ipa: /il i a œ̃ ɡʁɑ̃ li dɑ̃ la ʃɑ̃bʁ/
items.notes: The final "d" of "grand" and the final "t" of "lit" are both silent.

items.fr: Nous rangeons nos affaires chaque matin.
items.en: We put our things away every morning.
items.notes: Liaison links "nos" and "affaires" with a /z/ sound that has no letter of its own to add.

items.fr: Mon frère dort dans la petite chambre.
items.en: My brother sleeps in the small bedroom.
items.ipa: /mɔ̃ fʁɛʁ dɔʁ dɑ̃ la pə.tit ʃɑ̃bʁ/
items.notes: The final "e" of "petite" is silent, but it makes the preceding "t" audible, unlike masculine "petit".

items.fr: Le salon a deux fenêtres et une porte.
items.en: The living room has two windows and one door.
items.ipa: /lə sa.lɔ̃ a dø fə.nɛtʁ e yn pɔʁt/
items.notes: "et" (and) sounds exactly like "est" (is), so context alone tells you which spelling to use.

items.fr: Ma sœur balaie la cuisine tous les soirs.
items.en: My sister sweeps the kitchen every evening.
items.ipa: /ma sœʁ ba.lɛ la kɥi.zin tu le swaʁ/
items.notes: "balaie" keeps the "ai" spelling even though it sounds like a simple "è".

items.fr: Les rideaux sont bleus dans le salon.
items.en: The curtains are blue in the living room.
items.ipa: /le ʁi.do sɔ̃ blø dɑ̃ lə sa.lɔ̃/
items.notes: The final "x" of "rideaux" and the final "s" of "bleus" are both silent plural markers.

items.fr: Il ferme la fenêtre parce qu'il fait froid.
items.en: He closes the window because it is cold.
items.ipa: /il fɛʁm la fə.nɛtʁ paʁs.kil fɛ fʁwa/
items.notes: "que" drops its "e" before the vowel of "il", written as "qu'il".

items.fr: Nous avons un canapé confortable au salon.
items.en: We have a comfortable sofa in the living room.
items.notes: "Nous avons" is joined by a liaison /z/ even though "nous" ends in a silent "s".

items.fr: La salle de bain est au bout du couloir.
items.en: The bathroom is at the end of the hallway.
items.ipa: /la sal də bɛ̃ ɛ.t‿o bu dy ku.lwaʁ/
items.notes: "bain" is one single nasal sound, not "ba" plus a separate "n".

items.fr: Mes parents rangent le garage le samedi.
items.en: My parents tidy the garage on Saturdays.
items.ipa: /me pa.ʁɑ̃ ʁɑ̃ʒ lə ɡa.ʁaʒ lə sam.di/
items.notes: The "ent" ending of "rangent" is completely silent, just like most third person plural verb endings.

items.fr: On mange dans la cuisine ce soir.
items.en: We are eating in the kitchen tonight.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ mɑ̃ʒ dɑ̃ la kɥi.zin sə swaʁ/
items.notes: "on" (we, one) sounds identical to "ont" (they have), so only sentence sense tells you which to write.

items.fr: Le chat dort sur le grand lit blanc.
items.en: The cat sleeps on the big white bed.
items.ipa: /lə ʃa dɔʁ syʁ lə ɡʁɑ̃ li blɑ̃/
items.notes: The final consonants of "grand" and "blanc" are silent unless a liaison occurs.

items.fr: J'ouvre la porte de la cave doucement.
items.en: I open the cellar door slowly.
items.ipa: /ʒuvʁ la pɔʁt də la kav dus.mɑ̃/
items.notes: "je" loses its "e" before a vowel and becomes "j'" attached to "ouvre".

items.fr: Il y a beaucoup de bruit chez les voisins.
items.en: There is a lot of noise at the neighbors' place.
items.ipa: /il i a bo.ku də bʁɥi ʃe le vwa.zɛ̃/
items.notes: "beaucoup" combines the tricky spelling "eau" for /o/ with "ou" for /u/, easy to mix up when writing fast.

items.fr: Nous avons déménagé dans un nouvel appartement.
items.en: We moved into a new apartment.
items.notes: The past participle "déménagé" sounds identical to the infinitive "déménager", so the ending must be chosen from grammar, not sound.

items.fr: Elle a peint les murs du salon en bleu.
items.en: She painted the living room walls blue.
items.ipa: /ɛl a pɛ̃ le myʁ dy sa.lɔ̃ ɑ̃ blø/
items.notes: "peint" ends in a nasal sound with a silent final "t", an irregular past participle spelling.

items.fr: Nous allons repeindre la cuisine ce week-end.
items.en: We are going to repaint the kitchen this weekend.
items.notes: Liaison links "nous" and "allons" with a /z/ sound before the verb.

items.fr: Les voisins ont fait beaucoup de bruit hier soir.
items.en: The neighbors made a lot of noise last night.
items.ipa: /le vwa.zɛ̃ ɔ̃ fɛ bo.ku də bʁɥi jɛʁ swaʁ/
items.notes: "ont" (they have) sounds like "on", so check the plural subject "les voisins" to know it takes "ont".

items.fr: J'ai acheté des étagères pour la chambre.
items.en: I bought some shelves for the bedroom.
items.ipa: /ʒe aʃ.te de ze.ta.ʒɛʁ puʁ la ʃɑ̃bʁ/
items.notes: "acheté" ends in the same sound as the infinitive "acheter", so only the auxiliary "ai" shows it is a past participle.

items.fr: Où as-tu rangé les clés de la maison?
items.en: Where did you put the house keys?
items.ipa: /u a ty ʁɑ̃.ʒe le kle də la mɛ.zɔ̃/
items.notes: "où" (where, with accent) must not be confused with "ou" (or), even though both sound the same.

items.fr: Ma mère a nettoyé toute la maison ce matin.
items.en: My mother cleaned the whole house this morning.
items.ipa: /ma mɛʁ a nɛ.twa.je tut la mɛ.zɔ̃ sə ma.tɛ̃/
items.notes: "nettoyé" stays masculine singular because the direct object "la maison" comes after the verb, not before.

items.fr: Ils vont poser un nouveau parquet dans le couloir.
items.en: They are going to lay new flooring in the hallway.
items.ipa: /il vɔ̃ po.ze œ̃ nu.vo paʁ.kɛ dɑ̃ lə ku.lwaʁ/
items.notes: The final "t" of "vont" is silent, and "parquet" also ends in a silent "t".

items.fr: Nous avons enfin fini les travaux de la salle de bain.
items.en: We have finally finished the bathroom renovations.
items.ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃.z‿ɑ̃.fɛ̃ fi.ni le tʁa.vo də la sal də bɛ̃/
items.notes: Two liaisons in a row link "nous avons" and "avons enfin" with /z/ sounds.

items.fr: Le propriétaire va augmenter le loyer en janvier.
items.en: The landlord is going to raise the rent in January.
items.ipa: /lə pʁɔ.pʁi.je.tɛʁ va oɡ.mɑ̃.te lə lwa.je ɑ̃ ʒɑ̃.vje/
items.notes: "en" before a consonant makes a nasal sound with no separate "n" pronounced.

items.fr: Elle a déjà fini de ranger sa chambre.
items.en: She has already finished tidying her room.
items.ipa: /ɛl a de.ʒa fi.ni də ʁɑ̃.ʒe sa ʃɑ̃bʁ/
items.notes: "déjà" always keeps its grave accent on the final "a" even though nothing in the pronunciation signals it.

items.fr: Il faut que tu fasses le ménage ce week-end.
items.en: You need to do the housework this weekend.
items.ipa: /il fo kə ty fas lə me.naʒ sə wik.ɛnd/
items.notes: The subjunctive "fasses" replaces the indicative "fais" after "il faut que", an irregular form of "faire".

items.fr: Ces meubles ne sont pas très solides.
items.en: These pieces of furniture are not very sturdy.
items.ipa: /se mœbl nə sɔ̃ pa tʁɛ sɔ.lid/
items.notes: "ces" (these, demonstrative) sounds exactly like "ses" (his/her) and "c'est" (it is).

items.fr: Je pense que ce logement est trop cher pour nous.
items.en: I think this place is too expensive for us.
items.ipa: /ʒə pɑ̃s kə sə lɔʒ.mɑ̃ ɛ tʁo ʃɛʁ puʁ nu/
items.notes: "ce" (this, demonstrative adjective) is easily confused with the reflexive pronoun "se", even though no reflexive verb appears here.

items.fr: Quelle chambre préfères-tu, la grande ou la petite?
items.en: Which bedroom do you prefer, the big one or the small one?
items.ipa: /kɛl ʃɑ̃bʁ pʁe.fɛʁ ty la ɡʁɑ̃d u la pə.tit/
items.notes: "quelle" agrees in the feminine with "chambre" and sounds identical to "quel", "quels", and "quelles".

items.fr: Bien qu'il pleuve, nous devons réparer le toit aujourd'hui.
items.en: Even though it is raining, we have to repair the roof today.
items.ipa: /bjɛ̃ kil plœv nu də.vɔ̃ ʁe.pa.ʁe lə twa o.ʒuʁ.dɥi/
items.notes: "pleuve" is the irregular subjunctive form of "pleuvoir" required after "bien que".

items.fr: Les ouvriers viendront réparer la fuite dès qu'ils pourront.
items.en: The workers will come fix the leak as soon as they can.
items.ipa: /le.z‿u.vʁi.je vjɛ̃.dʁɔ̃ ʁe.pa.ʁe la fɥit dɛ kil puʁ.ʁɔ̃/
items.notes: The plural "s" of "ouvriers" stays silent because the next word "viendront" begins with a consonant, so no liaison occurs.

items.fr: Mon voisin est plus bruyant que je ne le pensais.
items.en: My neighbor is noisier than I thought.
items.ipa: /mɔ̃ vwa.zɛ̃ ɛ ply bʁɥi.jɑ̃ kə ʒə nə lə pɑ̃.sɛ/
items.notes: The string of mute e's in "que je ne le" is barely pronounced in fast speech, but every one must still be written.

items.fr: C'est le locataire qui doit payer les petites réparations.
items.en: It is the tenant who has to pay for the small repairs.
items.ipa: /sɛ lə lɔ.ka.tɛʁ ki dwa pe.je le pə.tit ʁe.pa.ʁa.sjɔ̃/
items.notes: "c'est" is easy to confuse with "s'est" or "ses" since all three sound the same.

items.fr: Je doute que ce studio soit assez grand pour deux.
items.en: I doubt this studio is big enough for two.
items.ipa: /ʒə dut kə sə sty.djo swa a.se ɡʁɑ̃ puʁ dø/
items.notes: "soit" is the subjunctive of "être" required after "je doute que", not to be confused with "soi" or "sois".

items.fr: Quand nous aurons fini les travaux, nous inviterons nos amis.
items.en: When we have finished the renovations, we will invite our friends.
items.ipa: /kɑ̃ nu.z‿o.ʁɔ̃ fi.ni le tʁa.vo nu.z‿ɛ̃.vi.tə.ʁɔ̃ no.z‿a.mi/
items.notes: Three separate liaisons link "nous aurons", "nous inviterons", and "nos amis" with /z/ sounds.

items.fr: Il semble que les clés aient été oubliées sur la table.
items.en: It seems the keys were forgotten on the table.
items.ipa: /il sɑ̃bl kə le kle ɛ.t‿e.te u.bli.je syʁ la tabl/
items.notes: "aient" is the subjunctive of "avoir", spelled with "-ent" though it is pronounced just like "est" or "es".

items.fr: Ses parents ont refait toute la toiture l'été dernier.
items.en: His parents redid the whole roof last summer.
items.ipa: /se pa.ʁɑ̃ ɔ̃ ʁə.fɛ tut la twa.tyʁ le.te dɛʁ.nje/
items.notes: "ses" (possessive) sounds the same as "ces" and "c'est" but has a different spelling and role.

items.fr: Nous cherchons un appartement où les charges sont incluses.
items.en: We are looking for an apartment where the utilities are included.
items.ipa: /nu ʃɛʁ.ʃɔ̃.z‿œ̃ na.paʁ.tə.mɑ̃ u le ʃaʁʒ sɔ̃.t‿ɛ̃.klyz/
items.notes: "où" keeps its accent because it means "where", unlike the conjunction "ou" meaning "or".

items.fr: Il vaudrait mieux que vous répariez la fenêtre avant l'hiver.
items.en: It would be better for you to fix the window before winter.
items.ipa: /il vo.dʁɛ mjø kə vu ʁe.pa.ʁje la fə.nɛtʁ a.vɑ̃ li.vɛʁ/
items.notes: The subjunctive ending "-iez" of "répariez" sounds close to the simple "-ez" ending, so it is easy to drop the extra "i".

items.fr: Les meubles que nous avons vendus étaient très anciens.
items.en: The furniture that we sold was very old.
items.ipa: /le mœbl kə nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ vɑ̃.dy e.tɛ tʁɛ.z‿ɑ̃.sjɛ̃/
items.notes: "vendus" takes a plural "s" to agree with "les meubles", the direct object placed before "avons vendu".

items.fr: La maison qu'ils ont achetée avait besoin de travaux.
items.en: The house they bought needed renovation work.
items.ipa: /la mɛ.zɔ̃ kil.z‿ɔ̃ aʃ.te.te a.vɛ bə.zwɛ̃ də tʁa.vo/
items.notes: "achetée" adds a silent feminine "e" to agree with "la maison", the preceding direct object of "ont acheté".
The final d of vend is silent, a common trap for this regular verb ending.

items.fr: S'il avait plu, nous n'aurions pas repeint la façade.
items.en: If it had rained, we would not have repainted the facade.
items.ipa: /sil a.vɛ ply nu no.ʁjɔ̃ pa ʁə.pɛ̃ la fa.sad/
items.notes: "si" elides to "s'" only before "il" or "ils", never before other pronouns like "elle".

items.fr: Bien qu'elle soit propriétaire, elle loue quand même une chambre.
items.en: Even though she is an owner, she still rents out a room.
items.ipa: /bjɛ̃ kɛl swa pʁɔ.pʁi.je.tɛʁ ɛl lu kɑ̃ mɛm yn ʃɑ̃bʁ/
items.notes: "que" elides before "elle" to become "qu'elle", pronounced as one syllable.

items.fr: Les clés que le locataire nous a rendues étaient rouillées.
items.en: The keys that the tenant gave back to us were rusty.
items.ipa: /le kle kə lə lɔ.ka.tɛʁ nu.z‿a ʁɑ̃.dy e.tɛ ʁu.je/
items.notes: "rendues" agrees with the feminine plural "les clés", the direct object placed before the auxiliary "a rendu".

items.fr: Si j'avais su, je n'aurais jamais signé ce bail.
items.en: If I had known, I would never have signed this lease.
items.ipa: /si ʒa.vɛ sy ʒə no.ʁɛ ʒa.mɛ si.ɲe sə baj/
items.notes: "je" elides before the vowel of "avais" to form "j'avais", one of several elisions in this sentence.

items.fr: Il faudrait que le propriétaire fasse changer la chaudière.
items.en: The landlord would need to have the boiler changed.
items.ipa: /il fo.dʁɛ kə lə pʁɔ.pʁi.je.tɛʁ fas ʃɑ̃.ʒe la ʃo.djɛʁ/
items.notes: "fasse" is the subjunctive form required after "il faudrait que", distinct from the indicative "fait" though both come from "faire".

items.fr: C'est le bruit des voisins du dessus qui l'empêche de dormir.
items.en: It is the noise from the upstairs neighbors that keeps him from sleeping.
items.ipa: /sɛ lə bʁɥi de vwa.zɛ̃ dy də.sy ki lɑ̃.pɛʃ də dɔʁ.miʁ/
items.notes: "le" elides to "l'" before the vowel of "empêche", merging into a single sound.

items.fr: Quoiqu'elle ait repeint tout le couloir, l'odeur de peinture persiste.
items.en: Although she repainted the whole hallway, the smell of paint lingers.
items.ipa: /kwa.kɛl ɛ ʁə.pɛ̃ tu lə ku.lwaʁ lo.dœʁ də pɛ̃.tyʁ pɛʁ.sist/
items.notes: "ait", the subjunctive of "avoir", sounds identical to "es", "est", and "ai" but is spelled differently.

items.fr: Les travaux que l'entreprise a entrepris coûtent plus cher que prévu.
items.en: The work that the company undertook costs more than expected.
items.ipa: /le tʁa.vo kə lɑ̃.tʁə.pʁiz a ɑ̃.tʁə.pʁi kut ply ʃɛʁ kə pʁe.vy/
items.notes: "entrepris" stays unchanged for masculine plural agreement because the base form already ends in "s".

items.fr: Il aurait fallu qu'on repeigne la chambre avant l'arrivée du bébé.
items.en: The bedroom should have been repainted before the baby's arrival.
items.ipa: /il o.ʁɛ fa.ly kɔ̃ ʁə.pɛɲ la ʃɑ̃bʁ a.vɑ̃ la.ʁi.ve dy be.be/
items.notes: "que" elides before "on" to form "qu'on", and "repeigne" is the irregular subjunctive of "repeindre".

items.fr: La décoration qu'elle a choisie correspond parfaitement au salon.
items.en: The decor she chose matches the living room perfectly.
items.ipa: /la de.kɔ.ʁa.sjɔ̃ kɛl a ʃwa.zi kɔ.ʁɛs.pɔ̃ paʁ.fɛt.mɑ̃ o sa.lɔ̃/
items.notes: "choisie" adds a feminine "e" because the preceding direct object "que" refers to "la décoration".

items.fr: Quels que soient les travaux, le propriétaire doit être prévenu.
items.en: Whatever the work involved, the landlord must be informed.
items.ipa: /kɛl kə swa.t‿le tʁa.vo lə pʁɔ.pʁi.je.tɛʁ dwa.t‿ɛtʁ pʁe.və.ny/
items.notes: "Quels que soient" requires the plural subjunctive "soient", agreeing with the plural "les travaux".

items.fr: Si nous avions loué un logement plus calme, nous aurions mieux dormi.
items.en: If we had rented a quieter place, we would have slept better.
items.ipa: /si nu.z‿a.vjɔ̃ lwe œ̃ lɔʒ.mɑ̃ ply kalm nu.z‿o.ʁjɔ̃ mjø dɔʁ.mi/
items.notes: Liaison links "nous avions" and "nous aurions" with /z/ sounds not shown by any letter of "nous".

items.fr: Le marché est ouvert le samedi matin.
items.en: The market is open on Saturday morning.
items.notes: Liaison between est and ouvert adds a t sound that is not heard when est stands alone.
Je elides to j' before the vowel-initial verb achète.

items.fr: Elle choisit des tomates bien mûres.
items.notes: The final t in choisit is silent, easy to forget when writing.
Pèse needs a grave accent to mark the open e sound, a detail invisible in casual speech.

items.en: How much does this cheese cost?
items.notes: Combien contains two nasal vowels that are easy to under-articulate when writing quickly.

items.en: We are looking for yellow flowers.
items.notes: Jaunes agrees in gender and number with fleurs, adding a silent final s.

items.fr: Vous voulez un kilo de carottes ?
items.en: Do you want a kilo of carrots?
items.notes: The unstressed e in de is a schwa that can fade in speech but must stay in writing.

items.fr: Ils achètent du pain à la boulangerie.
items.en: They buy bread at the bakery.
items.notes: Liaison between ils and achètent produces a z sound signaling the plural, not audible in il achète.

items.en: They look at the exotic fruits.
items.notes: The verb ending -ent in regardent is silent, so elle regarde and elles regardent sound almost identical.

items.fr: Je prends deux kilos de pommes de terre.
items.en: I am taking two kilos of potatoes.
items.ipa: /ʒə pʁɑ̃ dø ki.lo də pɔm də tɛʁ/
items.notes: The final ds in prends is silent, a common trap when writing present-tense verb forms.

items.fr: Le marchand rend la monnaie rapidement.
items.en: The merchant gives back the change quickly.
items.notes: Marchand, rend, and rapidement all contain nasal vowels that are easy to under-articulate when writing.
Lourde adds a feminine final e to agree with pastèque, a change not heard in speech.

items.fr: Les abricots sont chers cette semaine.
items.notes: Liaison between les and abricots adds a z sound marking the plural.

items.fr: On paie en espèces ou par carte.
items.en: We pay in cash or by card.
items.notes: Ou (or) has no accent, unlike its homophone où (where); context decides the spelling.

items.fr: Le client demande le prix des oranges.
items.en: The customer asks the price of the oranges.
items.ipa: /lə kli.jɑ̃ də.mɑ̃d lə pʁi de ɔ.ʁɑ̃ʒ/
items.notes: The final t in client is silent, a frequent spelling slip in dictée.

items.fr: La marchande sourit à ses clients.
items.en: The market woman smiles at her customers.
items.notes: À needs a grave accent to distinguish it from a (has), even though they sound the same.

items.fr: Les enfants aiment les fraises sucrées.
items.notes: Liaison between les and enfants adds a z that signals the plural article.

items.fr: Il y a beaucoup de monde au marché.
items.en: There are a lot of people at the market.
items.notes: The nasal vowel in monde is easy to under-pronounce, leading learners to drop the n when writing.

items.fr: Les pommes sont dans le panier.
items.en: The apples are in the basket.
items.notes: Dans ends in a nasal vowel that can be confused in spelling with dent or dents.

items.fr: Elle porte un grand sac de courses.
items.en: She is carrying a big shopping bag.
items.ipa: /ɛl pɔʁt œ̃ gʁɑ̃ sak də kuʁs/
items.notes: The final d of grand is silent before a consonant, unlike in liaison contexts.
Poissonnier doubles the n, a spelling detail not obvious from pronunciation.

items.fr: Nous achetons du fromage de chèvre.
items.notes: Liaison links nous and achetons with a z sound absent from the written words individually.
The -ent ending of sentent is silent, matching the plural subject without being heard.

items.fr: Je voudrais un kilo de cerises.
items.en: I would like a kilo of cherries.
items.notes: The schwa in je and de often disappears in fast speech but must remain in writing.

items.fr: Le fromager coupe une tranche de fromage.
items.en: The cheesemonger cuts a slice of cheese.
items.ipa: /lə fʁɔ.ma.ʒe kup yn tʁɑ̃ʃ də fʁɔ.maʒ/
items.notes: The -er ending of fromager is pronounced like é, a classic dictée confusion point.

items.fr: Les clients font la queue devant l'étal.
items.en: The customers wait in line in front of the stall.
items.ipa: /le kli.jɑ̃ fɔ̃ la kø də.vɑ̃ le.tal/
items.notes: Le étal elides to l'étal before the vowel-initial noun.

items.fr: Elle met les légumes dans son sac.
items.en: She puts the vegetables in her bag.
items.ipa: /ɛl mɛ le le.gym dɑ̃ sɔ̃ sak/
items.notes: Son (her) sounds identical to sont (are), so only meaning distinguishes the spelling.

items.fr: Le vendeur crie les prix du jour.
items.en: The seller calls out the day's prices.
items.ipa: /lə vɑ̃.dœʁ kʁi le pʁi dy ʒuʁ/
items.notes: The final x in prix is silent, easy to omit or misplace in dictée.
The circumflex on goûtons is silent but required in spelling, marking a lost historical s.
Vendent carries a nasal vowel followed by a silent -ent ending, both easy to misspell.
Liaison between deux and euros adds a z sound not present when deux stands alone.

items.fr: Ce raisin vient du sud de la France.
items.en: This grape comes from the south of France.
items.ipa: /sə ʁɛ.zɛ̃ vjɛ̃ dy syd də la fʁɑ̃s/
items.notes: Raisin ends in a nasal vowel that beginners often spell with an extra n.
Liaison after prix surfaces a z sound that the silent written x does not suggest.
Œufs in the plural loses the f sound heard in singular œuf, an irregular spelling-to-sound trap.
The final r of boucher is silent, following the standard -er ending pattern.

items.en: We are choosing a good melon.
items.notes: Un, bon, and melon all contain nasal vowels that are easy to under-articulate in dictée.

items.fr: Les asperges sont vertes et fines.
items.en: The asparagus are green and thin.
items.notes: Vertes and fines both add silent feminine plural endings to agree with asperges.

items.fr: Le marché ferme à treize heures.
items.en: The market closes at one o'clock.
items.notes: À carries an accent grave to distinguish it from a, though both are pronounced the same.

items.en: I love the smell of fresh bread.
items.notes: Both je and le elide before vowel-initial words, giving j'aime and l'odeur.

items.fr: Elle porte des sacs très lourds.
items.en: She is carrying very heavy bags.
items.notes: The final ds in lourds is completely silent, only visible in the written plural form.

items.fr: Les touristes visitent le marché local.
items.en: The tourists visit the local market.
items.notes: The silent -ent ending on visitent shows the plural subject without any audible change.

items.fr: Le vieux marchand connaît tous ses clients.
items.en: The old merchant knows all his customers.
items.ipa: /lə vjø maʁ.ʃɑ̃ kɔ.nɛ tu se kli.jɑ̃/
items.notes: Connaît keeps a circumflex accent on the i, a silent mark that must not be forgotten.

items.fr: Nous prenons un citron et deux oranges.
items.en: We are taking a lemon and two oranges.
items.notes: Citron ends in a nasal vowel often mis-transcribed with an extra n.

items.fr: Les champignons sont dans une petite boîte.
items.en: The mushrooms are in a small box.
items.notes: Boîte keeps a circumflex on the i, a silent accent that changes nothing in pronunciation but is required in spelling.

items.fr: Elle achète des épices pour la soupe.
items.en: She buys spices for the soup.
items.notes: Liaison between des and épices produces an audible z marking the plural.

items.fr: Le marché est près de l'église.
items.en: The market is near the church.
items.notes: La église elides to l'église because the noun begins with a vowel sound.
The silent -ent ending on goûtent signals a plural subject that cannot be heard.

items.fr: La marchande pèse les pommes une à une.
items.en: The market woman weighs the apples one by one.
items.ipa: /la maʁ.ʃɑ̃d pɛz le pɔm yn a yn/
items.notes: À needs its accent grave even though it sounds exactly like a (has).

items.fr: Les clients paient et partent vite.
items.en: The customers pay and leave quickly.
items.notes: Et (and) is a homophone of est (is); only the sentence meaning tells you which to write.

items.fr: Hier, j'ai acheté des fraises au marché.
items.en: Yesterday, I bought strawberries at the market.
items.ipa: /jɛʁ ʒe aʃ.te de fʁɛz o maʁ.ʃe/
items.notes: Acheté ends in a sound identical to acheter and achetez, so the ending must be chosen by grammar, not sound.

items.fr: Nous avons choisi les meilleurs fromages.
items.notes: Liaison between nous and avons adds a z sound not visible in either word alone.

items.fr: Elle a payé avec sa carte bancaire.
items.en: She paid with her bank card.
items.ipa: /ɛl a pɛ.je a.vɛk sa kaʁt bɑ̃.kɛʁ/
items.notes: Payé sounds the same as payer and payez, so the past participle ending relies on grammar, not sound.

items.fr: Ils sont allés au marché tôt le matin.
items.en: They went to the market early in the morning.
items.ipa: /il sɔ̃ a.le o maʁ.ʃe to lə ma.tɛ̃/
items.notes: Allés takes a silent plural s to agree with ils because it uses the auxiliary être.

items.fr: Le vendeur a pesé les tomates.
items.notes: Pesé ends in the same sound as peser, a frequent past participle confusion.

items.fr: Nous allons acheter du pain demain.
items.en: We are going to buy bread tomorrow.
items.notes: Liaison between nous and allons produces a z sound that signals the plural subject.

items.fr: Elle va goûter le fromage de chèvre.
items.en: She is going to taste the goat cheese.
items.ipa: /ɛl va gu.te lə fʁɔ.maʒ də ʃɛvʁ/
items.notes: The circumflex on goûter is silent but must be written, marking a historical lost s.

items.fr: Vous avez trouvé des fruits mûrs.
items.notes: Trouvé sounds identical to trouver and trouvez, so only grammar tells you which ending to write.

items.fr: Les enfants ont mangé toutes les cerises.
items.en: The children ate all the cherries.
items.notes: Ont (have) is a homophone of on (one), distinguished only by grammatical context.

items.fr: On a acheté beaucoup de légumes.
items.en: We bought a lot of vegetables.
items.notes: On sounds like ont, so writers must rely on meaning to choose the right spelling.

items.fr: Où as-tu trouvé ces belles fleurs ?
items.en: Where did you find these beautiful flowers?
items.ipa: /u a ty tʁu.ve se bɛl flœʁ/
items.notes: Où (where) carries an accent to distinguish it from ou (or), though both sound identical.

items.fr: Elle a demandé le prix des poires.
items.en: She asked the price of the pears.
items.ipa: /ɛl a də.mɑ̃.de lə pʁi de pwaʁ/
items.notes: Demandé ends the same as demander, a common past participle spelling trap.

items.fr: Nous avons marché longtemps entre les étals.
items.en: We walked for a long time between the stalls.
items.notes: Longtemps contains two nasal vowels and a silent final s, easy to misspell.

items.fr: Ils ont goûté les olives avant d'acheter.
items.en: They tasted the olives before buying.
items.notes: De acheter elides to d'acheter before the vowel-initial verb.

items.fr: Le marchand a donné la monnaie à Paul.
items.en: The merchant gave the change to Paul.
items.ipa: /lə maʁ.ʃɑ̃ a dɔ.ne la mɔ.nɛ a pɔl/
items.notes: The sentence contains both a (has) and à (to), which sound identical but are spelled differently.

items.fr: Elle a pris deux kilos de pommes.
items.en: She took two kilos of apples.
items.ipa: /ɛl a pʁi dø ki.lo də pɔm/
items.notes: The final s of the past participle pris is silent, easy to drop in dictée.

items.fr: On va négocier le prix du poisson.
items.en: We are going to negotiate the price of the fish.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ va ne.gɔ.sje lə pʁi dy pwa.sɔ̃/
items.notes: On and poisson both carry nasal vowels that beginners often under-pronounce when writing.

items.fr: Les clients ont fait la queue longtemps.
items.en: The customers waited in line for a long time.
items.ipa: /le kli.jɑ̃ ɔ̃ fɛ la kø lɔ̃.tɑ̃/
items.notes: Ont (have) must not be confused with its homophone on (one), a frequent dictée error.

items.fr: Il a vendu tous ses légumes ce matin.
items.en: He sold all his vegetables this morning.
items.ipa: /il a vɑ̃.dy tu se le.gym sə ma.tɛ̃/
items.notes: The final s of tous is silent before a consonant, unlike when it stands alone as a pronoun.

items.fr: Nous avons mis les fruits dans un sac.
items.en: We put the fruits in a bag.
items.notes: Dans and un both end in nasal vowels that liaison links with a z sound.

items.fr: Elle est arrivée tôt pour choisir les meilleurs produits.
items.en: She arrived early to choose the best products.
items.ipa: /ɛl ɛ.t‿a.ʁi.ve to puʁ ʃwa.ziʁ le mɛ.jœʁ pʁɔ.dɥi/
items.notes: Arrivée takes a silent feminine e to agree with elle since it uses the auxiliary être.

items.fr: Ils vont vendre des fleurs demain matin.
items.en: They are going to sell flowers tomorrow morning.
items.ipa: /il vɔ̃ vɑ̃dʁ de flœʁ də.mɛ̃ ma.tɛ̃/
items.notes: Vont ends in a nasal vowel and a silent t, distinct from words it merely resembles in speech.

items.fr: On a payé en espèces au marchand.
items.en: We paid in cash to the merchant.
items.notes: Payé sounds like payer, so the correct ending depends on recognizing the past participle form.

items.fr: Le boulanger a préparé du pain frais.
items.ipa: /lə bu.lɑ̃.ʒe a pʁe.pa.ʁe dy pɛ̃ fʁɛ/
items.notes: Préparé ends the same as préparer, requiring grammatical knowledge to spell correctly.

items.fr: Nous avons acheté du miel et des épices.
items.notes: Et (and) is a homophone of est (is), so context alone determines the correct spelling.

items.fr: Elle a comparé les prix entre deux étals.
items.en: She compared the prices between two stalls.
items.ipa: /ɛl a kɔ̃.pa.ʁe le pʁi ɑ̃.tʁə dø.z‿e.tal/
items.notes: Comparé sounds identical to comparer, another past-participle spelling trap.

items.en: Did they find a good cheesemonger?
items.notes: In this inverted question, ont must not be confused with its homophone on despite sounding alike.

items.fr: Le fromager a coupé une belle tranche.
items.en: The cheesemonger cut a nice slice.
items.ipa: /lə fʁɔ.ma.ʒe a ku.pe yn bɛl tʁɑ̃ʃ/
items.notes: Coupé ends the same as couper, a classic past participle versus infinitive confusion.

items.fr: Nous sommes passés devant le marché aux fleurs.
items.en: We passed by the flower market.
items.ipa: /nu sɔm pa.se də.vɑ̃ lə maʁ.ʃe o flœʁ/
items.notes: Passés adds a silent plural s to agree with the subject because it uses the auxiliary être.

items.fr: Elle a choisi de belles poires vertes.
items.en: She chose some nice green pears.
items.ipa: /ɛl a ʃwa.zi də bɛl pwaʁ vɛʁt/
items.notes: The past participle choisi ends in a silent i sound with no audible final consonant to guide spelling.

items.fr: Ils ont vendu leurs légumes très vite.
items.en: They sold their vegetables very quickly.
items.notes: Ont must be distinguished from its homophone on through the plural subject ils.

items.fr: On va acheter des asperges fraîches.
items.en: We are going to buy fresh asparagus.
items.notes: Liaison between des and asperges adds an audible z that marks the plural.

items.fr: Le marchand a baissé le prix des oranges.
items.en: The merchant lowered the price of the oranges.
items.ipa: /lə maʁ.ʃɑ̃ a bɛ.se lə pʁi de.z‿ɔ.ʁɑ̃ʒ/
items.notes: Baissé sounds the same as baisser, requiring the past participle ending to be chosen by grammar.

items.fr: Nous avons rapporté des légumes du marché.
items.en: We brought back vegetables from the market.
items.notes: Rapporté ends in the same sound as rapporter, another present infinitive versus past participle trap.
"Ils ont" liaises with a z-sound, unlike "il a", so the plural must be heard correctly.

items.en: My friends are looking for their glasses.
items.notes: "Mes amis" liaises with a z-sound that marks the plural you cannot skip in writing.

items.fr: Nous avons un petit sac noir.
items.en: We have a small black bag.
items.notes: "Nous avons" liaises with a z-sound linking into "un".

items.fr: Vous avez un beau parapluie aujourd'hui.
items.en: You have a beautiful umbrella today.
items.notes: "Vous avez" liaises with a z-sound between the pronoun and the verb.
"Elles ont" liaises with a z-sound, distinguishing it by ear from "elle a".

items.en: This is a very useful object.
items.notes: "C'est un" liaises with a t-sound, and "très utile" liaises with a z-sound.

items.fr: Ses lunettes sont sur le bureau.
items.en: Her glasses are on the desk.
items.notes: "Ses" sounds identical to "ces" and "c'est", so only context tells you which spelling to write.
"Où" (where) sounds exactly like "ou" (or), but only one of them takes an accent.

items.fr: C'est son sac, pas le mien.
items.en: This is his bag, not mine.
items.notes: "Son" (his/her) sounds identical to "sont" (are), so listen for the grammar, not just the sound.
"À" (belongs to) sounds exactly like "a" (has), so the accent must come from grammar, not sound.
"Ces" (these) sounds identical to "ses" (his/her), a classic dictée trap.

items.fr: Tu prends le sac ou la valise ?
items.en: Are you taking the bag or the suitcase?
items.ipa: /ty pʁɑ̃ lə sak u la va.liz/
items.notes: "Ou" (or) sounds exactly like "où" (where), but only "où" takes the accent.

items.fr: Le stylo est à côté du cahier.
items.en: The pen is next to the notebook.
items.ipa: /lə sti.lo ɛ a ko.te dy ka.je/
items.notes: The "à" in "à côté" sounds identical to "a", so the accent depends on grammar, not sound.
"Grandes" adds a silent -es to agree with the feminine plural "valises", a change you hear only from context.

items.fr: Mon sac est noir et ma veste est noire.
items.en: My bag is black and my jacket is black too.
items.ipa: /mɔ̃ sak ɛ nwaʁ e ma vɛst ɛ nwaʁ/
items.notes: "Noire" adds a silent -e to agree with the feminine "veste", though it sounds the same as "noir".
"Petits" adds a silent -s to agree with the plural "gants".
"Belle" doubles the letter l and adds -e to agree with the feminine "montre".
"Perdues" adds a silent -es to agree with the feminine plural "clés".
"Neuves" and "toutes" both carry silent feminine plural endings that agree with "lunettes".

items.fr: Le sac est lourd, la valise est lourde aussi.
items.en: The bag is heavy, the suitcase is heavy too.
items.ipa: /lə sak ɛ luʁ la va.liz ɛ luʁd o.si/
items.notes: "Lourde" adds a silent -e to agree with the feminine "valise", unlike the masculine "lourd".

items.fr: Mon téléphone est dans ma poche.
items.en: My phone is in my pocket.
items.notes: The nasal vowels in "mon" and "dans" must not be followed by a pronounced n or m sound.
The nasal vowels in "son" and "grand" sound similar but are spelled with different letters.

items.fr: Le vent est trop fort pour mon parapluie.
items.en: The wind is too strong for my umbrella.
items.ipa: /lə vɑ̃ ɛ tʁo fɔʁ puʁ mɔ̃ pa.ʁa.plɥi/
items.notes: "Vent" holds a nasal vowel spelled -ent, easy to confuse with the -an or -en spelling families.

items.en: I always have a white charger.
items.notes: "Un" and "blanc" both carry nasal vowels that sound alike but are spelled differently.
"Bien" holds a nasal vowel spelled -ien, distinct from the -in or -ain spelling families.
The nasal vowels in "gants" and "blancs" sound identical despite their different spellings.
The final "d" in "grand" is silent, easy to forget when writing.

items.en: I have an old grey pen.
items.notes: The final "s" in "gris" is silent, though the word sounds the same in singular and plural.
The final "p" in "trop" and the final "t" in "petit" are both silent.

items.en: I really like this old hat.
items.notes: The final "p" in "beaucoup" is silent and often mistakenly dropped or misplaced.

items.fr: Il range ses outils dans le fond du garage.
items.en: He puts his tools away at the back of the garage.
items.ipa: /il ʁɑ̃ʒ se zu.ti dɑ̃ lə fɔ̃ dy ga.ʁaʒ/
items.notes: The final "d" in "fond" is silent, though it resurfaces in related words like "fondamental".

items.fr: Mon vieux sac est vraiment lourd.
items.en: My old bag is really heavy.
items.notes: The final "d" in "lourd" is silent, only heard once a feminine -e is added.

items.en: I am buying a new umbrella today.
items.notes: "Aujourd'hui" starts with a silent h and hides an apostrophe that is easy to misplace.

items.en: My phone is staying at the hotel.
items.notes: "Hôtel" has a silent h and a circumflex accent marking a historically dropped letter.

items.fr: Il oublie souvent ses clés à l'école.
items.en: He often forgets his keys at school.
items.ipa: /il u.bli su.vɑ̃ se kle a le.kɔl/
items.notes: "École" carries an accent grave that changes the vowel and must be written, not just heard.

items.fr: Ma montre tombe souvent dans l'herbe.
items.en: My watch often falls in the grass.
items.notes: "Herbe" starts with a silent h that is never pronounced but always written.

items.fr: J'ai un joli collier en argent.
items.en: I have a pretty silver necklace.
items.notes: "Collier" doubles the letter l, a spelling that cannot be guessed from sound alone.

items.fr: J'ai un beau sac en cuir.
items.en: I have a beautiful leather bag.
items.notes: "Je" elides to "j'ai" before the vowel of "ai".

items.en: The computer is on the desk.
items.notes: "Le" elides to "l'" before the vowel of "ordinateur".

items.fr: C'est l'appareil photo de mon père.
items.notes: Both "ce" and "le" elide before vowels, giving "c'est l'appareil".

items.en: I really like this old watch.
items.notes: "Je" elides to "j'aime" before the vowel of "aime".
"La" elides to "l'" before the vowel of "écharpe".

items.en: She does not have a cell phone.
items.notes: "Ne" elides to "n'" before the vowel of "a".

items.fr: Le sac de Pierre est petit.
items.notes: The final -e of "petit" stays silent, but drop it and the word's meaning changes.

items.fr: La petite clé ouvre cette porte.
items.en: The little key opens this door.
items.notes: The unstressed e in "petite" is barely pronounced but never disappears in writing.

items.en: I am looking for a small watch.
items.notes: The e-muet in "je" can almost vanish in fast speech but must still be written.
The e-muet in "ne" is often dropped in speech but must appear in the written sentence.

items.fr: Je ne trouve pas mon sac.
items.notes: Both e-muets in "je" and "ne" can disappear in casual speech but must be written out.

items.fr: Le sac que tu portes est joli.
items.en: The bag you are carrying is nice.
items.ipa: /lə sak kə ty pɔʁt ɛ ʒɔ.li/
items.notes: The e-muet in "que" is easy to skip when listening but required in the spelling.

items.fr: La montre qu'elle a perdue était neuve.
items.en: The watch she lost was new.
items.ipa: /la mɔ̃tʁ kɛl a pɛʁ.dy e.tɛ nœv/
items.notes: The past participle "perdue" agrees with the feminine "montre" because the direct object comes before "avoir".

items.fr: Les clés qu'il a trouvées étaient sous le tapis.
items.en: The keys he found were under the rug.
items.ipa: /le kle kil a tʁu.ve e.tɛ su lə ta.pi/
items.notes: "Trouvées" agrees with the feminine plural "clés" placed before the auxiliary "avoir".

items.fr: Elle est allée chercher son sac à la gare.
items.en: She went to get her bag at the station.
items.ipa: /ɛl ɛt a.le ʃɛʁ.ʃe sɔ̃ sak a la gaʁ/
items.notes: With "être", the past participle "allée" agrees with the feminine subject "elle".

items.fr: Ils sont partis sans leurs valises.
items.notes: With "être", the past participle "partis" agrees with the masculine plural subject "ils".

items.fr: La valise que j'ai achetée est très lourde.
items.en: The suitcase I bought is very heavy.
items.ipa: /la va.liz kə ʒe aʃ.te ɛ tʁɛ luʁd/
items.notes: "Achetée" agrees with the feminine "valise" because the direct object precedes the auxiliary "avoir".

items.fr: On a oublié le sac à la gare.
items.en: We forgot the bag at the station.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ na u.bli.je lə sak a la gaʁ/
items.notes: "A" (has) and "à" (at) sound identical, so the accent depends entirely on grammar.

items.fr: Ils ont perdu leurs clés dans le taxi.
items.en: They lost their keys in the taxi.
items.ipa: /il zɔ̃ pɛʁ.dy lœʁ kle dɑ̃ lə tak.si/
items.notes: "Ont" (have) sounds exactly like "on" (one/we), a frequent listening trap.

items.fr: On a mis longtemps à retrouver ce portefeuille.
items.en: It took us a long time to find this wallet.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ na mi lɔ̃.tɑ̃ a ʁə.tʁu.ve sə pɔʁ.tə.fœj/
items.notes: "On" sounds identical to "ont", so only the surrounding verb form shows which one is correct.

items.fr: Tu sais où j'ai mis mon chargeur ?
items.en: Do you know where I put my charger?
items.ipa: /ty sɛ u ʒe mi mɔ̃ ʃaʁ.ʒœʁ/
items.notes: "Où" (where) sounds exactly like "ou" (or), but only "où" carries the accent.

items.fr: Elle cherche son parapluie ou son sac.
items.en: She is looking for her umbrella or her bag.
items.ipa: /ɛl ʃɛʁʃ sɔ̃ pa.ʁa.plɥi u sɔ̃ sak/
items.notes: "Ou" (or) sounds identical to "où" (where), a pair every dictée tests.

items.fr: Nous avons acheté un nouvel appareil photo.
items.ipa: /nu za.vɔ̃ zaʃ.te œ̃ nu.vɛl a.pa.ʁɛj fɔ.to/
items.notes: "Nouvel" replaces "nouveau" before a vowel, and "avons" liaises with a z-sound into "acheté".

items.fr: Elles ont retrouvé leurs affaires perdues.
items.notes: "Elles ont" liaises with a z-sound, distinguishing the plural from "elle a" by ear alone.

items.fr: Vous allez oublier vos clés encore une fois.
items.en: You are going to forget your keys again.
items.ipa: /vu za.le u.bli.je vo kle ɑ̃.kɔʁ yn fwa/
items.notes: "Vous allez" liaises with a z-sound linking the pronoun into "allez".

items.fr: Ils vont acheter un nouveau sac demain.
items.en: They are going to buy a new bag tomorrow.
items.ipa: /il vɔ̃t aʃ.te œ̃ nu.vo sak də.mɛ̃/
items.notes: "Ils vont" liaises with a t-sound before the vowel of "acheter".

items.fr: Il va ranger ses instruments dans un tiroir.
items.en: He is going to put his instruments away in a drawer.
items.ipa: /il va ʁɑ̃.ʒe se zɛ̃s.tʁy.mɑ̃ dɑ̃ zœ̃ ti.ʁwaʁ/
items.notes: The nasal vowels in "instruments" and "un" sound alike despite their different spellings.

items.fr: Elle a mis son téléphone dans un tiroir fermé.
items.en: She put her phone in a closed drawer.
items.ipa: /ɛl a mi sɔ̃ te.le.fɔn dɑ̃ zœ̃ ti.ʁwaʁ fɛʁ.me/
items.notes: The nasal vowels in "son" and "un" must be told apart by spelling, not by sound.

items.fr: Nous allons emprunter ce parapluie demain matin.
items.en: We are going to borrow this umbrella tomorrow morning.
items.ipa: /nu za.lɔ̃ ɑ̃.pʁœ̃.te sə pa.ʁa.plɥi də.mɛ̃ ma.tɛ̃/
items.notes: "Emprunter" packs two nasal vowels close together, easy to blur when writing.

items.fr: J'ai rangé mon ordinateur dans un grand sac.
items.en: I put my computer away in a big bag.
items.ipa: /ʒe ʁɑ̃.ʒe mɔ̃n ɔʁ.di.na.tœʁ dɑ̃ zœ̃ gʁɑ̃ sak/
items.notes: The nasal vowels in "mon", "un", and "grand" all sound similar but use different spellings.

items.fr: Elle a rangé son sac dans le grand placard.
items.en: She put her bag away in the big cupboard.
items.ipa: /ɛl a ʁɑ̃.ʒe sɔ̃ sak dɑ̃ lə gʁɑ̃ pla.kaʁ/
items.notes: The final "d" in "grand" stays silent even though it is always written.

items.fr: Il a acheté un chargeur pas cher du tout.
items.en: He bought a very cheap charger.
items.ipa: /il a aʃ.te œ̃ ʃaʁ.ʒœʁ pa ʃɛʁ dy tu/
items.notes: The final "t" in "tout" is silent, a common source of missing letters in dictée.

items.fr: Nous avons cherché ses outils partout dans le garage.
items.en: We looked for his tools everywhere in the garage.
items.ipa: /nu za.vɔ̃ ʃɛʁ.ʃe se zu.ti paʁ.tu dɑ̃ lə ga.ʁaʒ/
items.notes: The final "t" in "partout" is silent, a common dictée slip.

items.fr: J'ai payé trop cher pour ce sac.
items.en: I paid too much for this bag.
items.ipa: /ʒe pe.je tʁo ʃɛʁ puʁ sə sak/
items.notes: The final "p" in "trop" is silent, easy to forget when spelling the word.

items.fr: J'ai acheté une nouvelle montre à l'aéroport.
items.en: I bought a new watch at the airport.
items.ipa: /ʒe aʃ.te yn nu.vɛl mɔ̃tʁ a la.e.ʁɔ.pɔʁ/
items.notes: "Aéroport" carries an accent aigu on the first e that must be written even though it is fully pronounced.

items.fr: Elle a laissé ses clés à l'hôtel ce matin.
items.en: She left her keys at the hotel this morning.
items.ipa: /ɛl a le.se se kle a lo.tɛl sə ma.tɛ̃/
items.notes: "Hôtel" has a silent h and a circumflex accent marking a historically missing letter.

items.fr: Nous avons acheté de nouveaux outils ce matin.
items.en: We bought new tools this morning.
items.ipa: /nu za.vɔ̃ zaʃ.te də nu.vo zu.ti sə ma.tɛ̃/
items.notes: The plural ending -eaux in "nouveaux" is silent but cannot be replaced with a simple -s.

items.fr: J'ai trouvé une clé cassée dans l'herbe.
items.en: I found a broken key in the grass.
items.ipa: /ʒe tʁu.ve yn kle ka.se dɑ̃ lɛʁb/
items.notes: "Cassée" doubles the letter s, and "herbe" begins with a silent h.

items.fr: J'ai emprunté l'ordinateur de mon frère.
items.notes: "Le" elides to "l'" before the vowel of "ordinateur".

items.fr: Elle n'a pas retrouvé son sac.
items.en: She did not find her bag.
items.notes: "Ne" elides to "n'" before the vowel of "a".

items.fr: Il va s'acheter un nouveau portable.
items.en: He is going to buy himself a new cell phone.
items.notes: The reflexive "se" elides to "s'" before the vowel of "acheter".

items.fr: L'appareil photo de Julie est cassé.
items.notes: "Le" elides to "l'" before the vowel of "appareil".

items.fr: Je vais chercher mon petit sac demain.
items.en: I am going to get my small bag tomorrow.
items.ipa: /ʒə vɛ ʃɛʁ.ʃe mɔ̃ pə.ti sak də.mɛ̃/
items.notes: The e-muet in "je" is barely heard but must still appear in writing.

items.fr: Elle ne retrouve plus sa clé.
items.en: She can no longer find her key.
items.notes: The e-muet in "ne" often disappears in fast speech but is required in the spelling.

items.fr: Nous allons acheter une petite lampe.
items.en: We are going to buy a small lamp.
items.notes: The unstressed e in "petite" is barely pronounced but never disappears from the written word.

items.fr: Il ne sait plus où se trouve son sac.
items.en: He no longer knows where his bag is.
items.ipa: /il nə sɛ ply u sə tʁuv sɔ̃ sak/
items.notes: The e-muets in "ne" and "se" are easy to drop by ear but must be written in full.

items.fr: Nous nous levons tôt le week-end aussi.
items.en: We get up early on weekends too.
items.ipa: /nu nu ləvɔ̃ to lə wikɛnd osi/
items.notes: The two consecutive 'nous' before a reflexive verb are easy to merge into one when writing quickly.

example.en: The stapler is on the desk.
example.fr: L'agrafeuse est sur le bureau.

items.fr: Il se lave les mains avant le repas.
items.en: He washes his hands before the meal.
items.ipa: /il sə lav le mɛ̃ avɑ̃ lə ʁəpa/
items.notes: The nasal vowel in 'mains' is spelled with -ains but sounds like a single nasal vowel.

items.fr: Nous prenons le petit déjeuner ensemble.
items.notes: The final t in 'petit' is silent here since no liaison occurs before the consonant sound of 'déjeuner'.

items.fr: Elle se brosse les dents après le petit déjeuner.
items.en: She brushes her teeth after breakfast.
items.ipa: /ɛl sə bʁɔs le dɑ̃ apʁɛ lə pəti deʒøne/
items.notes: 'Dents' sounds identical to 'dans', so listeners must rely on context to spell it correctly.

items.fr: Tu prends ta douche le matin.
items.en: You take your shower in the morning.
items.notes: The final d in 'prends' is silent, which can tempt learners to drop the letter entirely when writing.

items.fr: Nous allons à l'école à huit heures.
items.en: We go to school at eight o'clock.
items.notes: The liaison in 'huit heures' pronounces the t of 'huit' before the vowel of 'heures'.

items.fr: Je bois un café avant de partir.
items.en: I drink a coffee before leaving.
items.ipa: /ʒə bwa œ̃ kafe avɑ̃ də paʁtiʁ/
items.notes: The nasal vowel in 'un' must be written with the silent n, not just the vowel sound alone.

items.fr: Il met son manteau et ses chaussures.
items.en: He puts on his coat and his shoes.
items.ipa: /il mɛ sɔ̃ mɑ̃to e se ʃosyʁ/
items.notes: 'Ses' sounds exactly like 'ces', so spelling depends on recognizing the possessive meaning.

items.fr: Elle prend le bus pour aller au travail.
items.en: She takes the bus to go to work.
items.ipa: /ɛl pʁɑ̃ lə bys puʁ ale o tʁavaj/
items.notes: The final d of 'prend' is never pronounced, a common source of spelling slips in dictation.

items.fr: Nous marchons jusqu'à la gare tous les jours.
items.en: We walk to the station every day.
items.ipa: /nu maʁʃɔ̃ ʒyska la ɡaʁ tu le ʒuʁ/
items.notes: Before a plural noun, 'tous' is pronounced without its final s, unlike when it stands alone as a pronoun.

items.fr: Je déjeune à midi avec mes collègues.
items.en: I have lunch at noon with my colleagues.
items.ipa: /ʒə deʒøn a midi avɛk me kɔlɛɡ/
items.notes: The unstressed e in 'je' is a mute e that learners sometimes drop or add incorrectly in writing.

items.fr: Il travaille dans un bureau au centre-ville.
items.en: He works in an office downtown.
items.ipa: /il tʁavaj dɑ̃ zœ̃ byʁo o sɑ̃tʁəvil/
items.notes: The liaison between 'dans' and 'un' produces a z sound that must not be written as an extra letter.

items.fr: Elle rentre chez elle vers dix-huit heures.
items.en: She goes home around six p.m.
items.notes: The liaison chain in 'dix-huit heures' links three sounds together and can obscure the correct spelling of each number.

items.en: We have dinner together in the evening.
items.notes: 'Ensemble' begins with a nasal vowel spelled en, easily confused with an or in when written from sound alone.

items.fr: Je regarde la télévision avant de dormir.
items.ipa: /ʒə ʁəɡaʁd la televizjɔ̃ avɑ̃ də dɔʁmiʁ/
items.notes: The mute e in 'regarde' is rarely pronounced but must still appear in the spelling.

items.fr: Il se couche tôt pendant la semaine.
items.en: He goes to bed early during the week.
items.ipa: /il sə kuʃ to pɑ̃dɑ̃ la səmɛn/
items.notes: The final t in 'tôt' is completely silent, so learners must remember it exists only in writing.

items.fr: Elle éteint la lumière avant de s'endormir.
items.en: She turns off the light before falling asleep.
items.ipa: /ɛl etɛ̃ la lymjɛʁ avɑ̃ də sɑ̃dɔʁmiʁ/
items.notes: 'Éteint' ends in a nasal vowel sound that is spelled -eint, not with a simple n.

items.fr: Tu ranges ta chambre chaque matin.
items.en: You tidy your room every morning.
items.notes: Both 'ranges' and 'chambre' contain the nasal vowel spelled an, which can be mistaken for en.

items.fr: Je prépare le déjeuner pour les enfants.
items.en: I prepare lunch for the children.
items.ipa: /ʒə pʁepaʁ lə deʒøne puʁ le zɑ̃fɑ̃/
items.notes: The liaison in 'les enfants' adds a z sound between the words that is not written as a separate letter.

items.fr: Elle part au travail à pied.
items.en: She leaves for work on foot.
items.notes: The final d in 'pied' is silent, a frequent trap since many other words ending in d behave the same way.

items.fr: Nous faisons les courses le samedi matin.
items.en: We do the shopping on Saturday morning.
items.ipa: /nu fəzɔ̃ le kuʁs lə samdi matɛ̃/
items.notes: 'Faisons' is pronounced with a schwa sound even though it is spelled with ai, an irregular pattern to memorize.

items.fr: Je me douche avant de m'habiller.
items.notes: The silent h in 'habiller' still triggers elision, so 'me' becomes m'habiller in writing.

items.fr: Il attend le bus devant chez lui.
items.en: He waits for the bus in front of his house.
items.ipa: /il atɑ̃ lə bys dəvɑ̃ ʃe lɥi/
items.notes: The final d in 'attend' is silent, matching the pattern of other present-tense endre verbs.

items.fr: Elle mange une pomme après le déjeuner.
items.en: She eats an apple after lunch.
items.ipa: /ɛl mɑ̃ʒ yn pɔm apʁɛ lə deʒøne/
items.notes: 'Une' must agree with the feminine noun 'pomme', not the masculine 'un', even though pomme starts with a consonant.

items.fr: Nous rangeons la cuisine après le dîner.
items.en: We tidy the kitchen after dinner.
items.ipa: /nu ʁɑ̃ʒɔ̃ la kɥizin apʁɛ lə dine/
items.notes: 'Rangeons' keeps an extra e before -ons to preserve the soft g sound, an irregular spelling rule for -ger verbs.

items.fr: Je sors du travail à dix-sept heures.
items.en: I leave work at five p.m.
items.ipa: /ʒə sɔʁ dy tʁavaj a diz sɛt‿œʁ/
items.notes: The liaison in 'dix-sept heures' pronounces the final consonants of both number words before the vowel.

items.fr: Elle se repose un peu avant le dîner.
items.en: She rests a little before dinner.
items.ipa: /ɛl sə ʁəpoz œ̃ pø avɑ̃ lə dine/
items.notes: The nasal vowel in 'un' is a single sound but requires writing both the vowel and the silent n.

items.fr: Nous éteignons les lumières en partant.
items.en: We turn off the lights when leaving.
items.notes: 'Éteignons' contains the gn sound spelled with ign, which is easy to misspell as in or ein.

items.fr: Ce matin, je me suis levé tôt pour aller courir.
items.en: This morning, I got up early to go running.
items.ipa: /sə matɛ̃ ʒə mə sɥi ləve to puʁ ale kuʁiʁ/
items.notes: The past participle 'levé' agrees with the reflexive subject, so a female speaker would need to add an e.

items.fr: Elle s'est habillée rapidement avant de sortir.
items.en: She got dressed quickly before going out.
items.ipa: /ɛl sɛ abije ʁapidmɑ̃ avɑ̃ də sɔʁtiʁ/
items.notes: 'Habillée' takes an extra e to agree with the feminine subject elle in this reflexive construction.

items.fr: Nous nous sommes réveillés en retard ce matin.
items.en: We woke up late this morning.
items.ipa: /nu nu sɔm ʁevɛje ɑ̃ ʁətaʁ sə matɛ̃/
items.notes: The past participle 'réveillés' takes a plural s to agree with the plural reflexive subject nous.

items.fr: Il a pris son petit déjeuner puis il est parti travailler.
items.en: He had his breakfast then he left for work.
items.ipa: /il a pʁi sɔ̃ pəti deʒøne pɥi il ɛ paʁti tʁavaje/
items.notes: 'Puis' sounds identical to 'puits', so only the sentence meaning confirms the correct spelling.

items.fr: Je vais me préparer avant de partir au bureau.
items.en: I am going to get ready before leaving for the office.
items.ipa: /ʒə vɛ mə pʁepaʁe avɑ̃ də paʁtiʁ o byʁo/
items.notes: The infinitive 'préparer' ending in -er sounds just like a past participle in -é, a common futur proche trap.

items.fr: Elle a mangé son déjeuner, ensuite elle a fait la vaisselle.
items.en: She ate her lunch, then she did the dishes.
items.ipa: /ɛl a mɑ̃ʒe sɔ̃ deʒøne ɑ̃sɥit ɛl a fɛ la vɛsɛl/
items.notes: 'Ensuite' opens with the nasal vowel en, which learners often confuse with an when writing from dictation.

items.fr: Nous avons pris le métro puis nous avons marché jusqu'au bureau.
items.en: We took the metro then we walked to the office.
items.ipa: /nu zavɔ̃ pʁi lə metʁo pɥi nu zavɔ̃ maʁʃe ʒysko byʁo/
items.notes: The liaison in 'nous avons' adds a z sound that links the words but is not a separate written letter.

items.fr: Ils se sont couchés très tard hier soir.
items.en: They went to bed very late last night.
items.ipa: /il sə sɔ̃ kuʃe tʁɛ taʁ jɛʁ swaʁ/
items.notes: 'Couchés' takes a plural s to agree with the plural reflexive subject ils.

items.fr: Après le travail, je vais faire les courses.
items.en: After work, I am going to do the shopping.
items.ipa: /apʁɛ lə tʁavaj ʒə vɛ fɛʁ le kuʁs/
items.notes: The final s in 'vais' is silent, following the regular pattern of first-person present-tense verb endings.

items.fr: Elle a oublié son sac au bureau ce matin.
items.en: She forgot her bag at the office this morning.
items.ipa: /ɛl a ublije sɔ̃ sak o byʁo sə matɛ̃/
items.notes: The verb form 'a' is easily confused in sound with the preposition 'à', though their spellings differ.

items.fr: Nous allons dîner ensemble puis regarder un film.
items.en: We are going to have dinner together then watch a movie.
items.ipa: /nu zalɔ̃ dine ɑ̃sɑ̃bl pɥi ʁəɡaʁde œ̃ film/
items.notes: The nasal vowel in 'un' before 'film' must be written with the silent n even though only one sound is heard.

items.fr: Il s'est brossé les dents avant de se coucher.
items.en: He brushed his teeth before going to bed.
items.ipa: /il sɛ bʁɔse le dɑ̃ avɑ̃ də sə kuʃe/
items.notes: 'Brossé' stays masculine singular here because the direct object dents follows the verb rather than preceding it.

items.fr: Ce soir, nous allons nous coucher plus tôt.
items.en: Tonight, we are going to go to bed earlier.
items.ipa: /sə swaʁ nu zalɔ̃ nu kuʃe ply to/
items.notes: The final s in 'plus' is silent in this context, unlike when plus means additionally at the end of a phrase.

items.fr: Elle a pris sa douche, puis elle s'est habillée pour sortir.
items.en: She took her shower, then she got dressed to go out.
items.ipa: /ɛl a pʁi sa duʃ pɥi ɛl sɛ abije puʁ sɔʁtiʁ/
items.notes: 'Habillée' agrees in gender with elle, adding a silent e that changes the spelling but not the sound.

items.fr: Nous avons fini nos devoirs avant le dîner.
items.en: We finished our homework before dinner.
items.ipa: /nu zavɔ̃ fini no dəvwaʁ avɑ̃ lə dine/
items.notes: The liaison in 'nous avons' produces a z sound bridging the two words in speech.

items.fr: Demain, je vais me lever plus tôt que d'habitude.
items.en: Tomorrow, I am going to get up earlier than usual.
items.ipa: /dəmɛ̃ ʒə vɛ mə ləve ply to kə dabityd/
items.notes: The silent h in 'habitude' still causes elision, turning de habitude into d'habitude in writing.

items.fr: Ils ont quitté la maison sans prendre de petit déjeuner.
items.en: They left the house without having breakfast.
items.ipa: /il zɔ̃ kite la mɛzɔ̃ sɑ̃ pʁɑ̃dʁ də pəti deʒøne/
items.notes: The liaison in 'ils ont' produces a z sound linking the pronoun to the verb.

items.fr: Quand j'étais petit, je me levais toujours à la même heure.
items.en: When I was little, I always got up at the same time.
items.ipa: /kɑ̃ ʒetɛ pəti ʒə mə ləvɛ tuʒuʁ a la mɛm œʁ/
items.notes: The imparfait ending -ais in 'levais' sounds identical to other imparfait and conditional endings, so spelling relies on tense recognition.

items.fr: Il faut que tu te lèves avant huit heures demain.
items.en: You need to get up before eight o'clock tomorrow.
items.ipa: /il fo kə ty tə lɛv avɑ̃ ɥit‿œʁ dəmɛ̃/
items.notes: The subjunctive form 'lèves' looks like the present indicative but is triggered by the expression il faut que.

items.fr: Ce sont ses habitudes du matin qu'elle ne change jamais.
items.en: These are her morning habits that she never changes.
items.ipa: /sə sɔ̃ se abityd dy matɛ̃ kɛl nə ʃɑ̃ʒ ʒamɛ/
items.notes: 'Ce' and 'se' sound alike, as do 'ses' and 'ces', so context alone determines the correct spelling in this sentence.

items.fr: Quelle heure est-il quand tu pars travailler le matin?
items.en: What time is it when you leave for work in the morning?
items.ipa: /kɛl œʁ ɛt il kɑ̃ ty paʁ tʁavaje lə matɛ̃/
items.notes: 'Quelle' sounds identical to 'quel' and to 'qu'elle', so agreement with heure must guide the spelling.

items.fr: Bien qu'il soit fatigué, il se lève toujours à six heures.
items.en: Although he is tired, he always gets up at six o'clock.
items.ipa: /bjɛ̃ kil swa fatiɡe il sə lɛv tuʒuʁ a si zœʁ/
items.notes: The subjunctive 'soit' is triggered by bien que and sounds different from the indicative est only in context.

items.fr: Avant, je prenais le train, mais maintenant je conduis.
items.en: Before, I used to take the train, but now I drive.
items.ipa: /avɑ̃ ʒə pʁənɛ lə tʁɛ̃ mɛ mɛ̃tnɑ̃ ʒə kɔ̃dɥi/
items.notes: The imparfait 'prenais' marks a past habit and must not be confused in spelling with the present tense prends.

items.fr: Elle se demande si elle a le temps de déjeuner avant de partir.
items.en: She wonders if she has time to have lunch before leaving.
items.ipa: /ɛl sə dəmɑ̃d si ɛl a lə tɑ̃ də deʒøne avɑ̃ də paʁtiʁ/
items.notes: 'Temps' sounds like 'tant' and 'tend', so its spelling can only be confirmed through meaning.

items.fr: Il faut que nous soyons prêts avant que le bus arrive.
items.en: We need to be ready before the bus arrives.
items.ipa: /il fo kə nu swajɔ̃ pʁɛ avɑ̃ kə lə bys aʁiv/
items.notes: The subjunctive form 'soyons' replaces the expected sommes after the expression il faut que.

items.fr: Chaque matin, elle se demandait ce qu'elle allait préparer pour le dîner.
items.en: Every morning, she wondered what she was going to prepare for dinner.
items.ipa: /ʃak matɛ̃ ɛl sə dəmɑ̃dɛ sə kɛl alɛ pʁepaʁe puʁ lə dine/
items.notes: 'Ce' in 'ce qu'elle' is often confused with the reflexive pronoun 'se' when writing from dictation.

items.fr: Dès qu'il se réveille, il vérifie son téléphone.
items.en: As soon as he wakes up, he checks his phone.
items.ipa: /dɛ kil sə ʁevɛj il veʁifi sɔ̃ telefɔn/
items.notes: The elision in 'qu'il' merges que and il into a single written unit that must not be separated.

items.fr: Autrefois, nous prenions toujours le petit déjeuner ensemble avant l'école.
items.en: In the past, we always used to have breakfast together before school.
items.ipa: /otʁəfwa nu pʁənjɔ̃ tuʒuʁ lə pəti deʒøne ɑ̃sɑ̃bl avɑ̃ lekɔl/
items.notes: The imparfait ending -ions in 'prenions' is a distinct written form that some learners simplify to -ons by mistake.

items.fr: Il est important que tu te couches tôt avant un examen.
items.en: It is important that you go to bed early before an exam.
items.ipa: /il ɛ ɛ̃pɔʁtɑ̃ kə ty tə kuʃ to avɑ̃ œ̃n‿ɛɡzamɛ̃/
items.notes: The liaison in 'un examen' links the n sound to the vowel, while 'couches' takes the subjunctive form triggered by il est important que.

items.fr: Le week-end, elle se levait plus tard que pendant la semaine.
items.en: On weekends, she used to get up later than during the week.
items.ipa: /lə wikɛnd ɛl sə ləvɛ ply taʁ kə pɑ̃dɑ̃ la səmɛn/
items.notes: The imparfait 'levait' can be mistaken for the present tense 'lève' since both are unstressed in rapid speech.

items.fr: Quel que soit le jour, il suit toujours la même routine.
items.en: Whatever the day, he always follows the same routine.
items.ipa: /kɛl kə swa lə ʒuʁ il sɥi tuʒuʁ la mɛm ʁutin/
items.notes: 'Quel' agrees with the masculine noun jour, and 'soit' is the subjunctive form required after quel que.

items.fr: Nous nous sommes habitués à nous lever tôt depuis que nous avons changé de travail.
items.en: We have gotten used to getting up early since we changed jobs.
items.ipa: /nu nu sɔm zabitɥe a nu ləve to dəpɥi kə nu zavɔ̃ ʃɑ̃ʒe də tʁavaj/
items.notes: The past participle 'habitués' takes a plural s to agree with the plural reflexive subject nous.

items.fr: Il se peut qu'elle soit déjà partie travailler.
items.en: It is possible that she has already left for work.
items.ipa: /il sə pø kɛl swa deʒa paʁti tʁavaje/
items.notes: The subjunctive 'soit' follows the impersonal expression il se peut que, not the indicative est.

items.fr: Ce n'est pas la même chose de se lever tôt en semaine et le week-end.
items.en: It is not the same thing to get up early on weekdays and on weekends.
items.ipa: /sə nɛ pa la mɛm ʃoz də sə ləve to ɑ̃ səmɛn e lə wikɛnd/
items.notes: 'Ce' at the start and 'se' before lever sound alike but serve completely different grammatical roles.

items.fr: Bien que je sois fatigué le matin, je fais toujours du sport avant le travail.
items.en: Although I am tired in the morning, I always do sports before work.
items.ipa: /bjɛ̃ kə ʒə swa fatiɡe lə matɛ̃ ʒə fɛ tuʒuʁ dy spɔʁ avɑ̃ lə tʁavaj/
items.notes: The subjunctive 'sois' after bien que replaces the expected indicative suis.

items.fr: Elle a changé sa routine depuis qu'elle travaille à domicile.
items.en: She has changed her routine since she has been working from home.
items.ipa: /ɛl a ʃɑ̃ʒe sa ʁutin dəpɥi kɛl tʁavaj a dɔmisil/
items.notes: The elision in 'qu'elle' joins que and elle into one written word before a vowel sound.

items.fr: Quelles que soient ses habitudes, elle arrive toujours à l'heure.
items.en: Whatever her habits are, she always arrives on time.
items.ipa: /kɛl kə swa se abityd ɛl aʁiv tuʒuʁ a lœʁ/
items.notes: The plural subjunctive 'soient' agrees with habitudes, and 'quelles' must match its feminine plural gender.

items.fr: Autrefois, il se réveillait sans réveil, mais maintenant il en a besoin.
items.en: In the past, he used to wake up without an alarm clock, but now he needs one.
items.ipa: /otʁəfwa il sə ʁevɛjɛ sɑ̃ ʁevɛj mɛ mɛ̃tnɑ̃ il ɑ̃n a bəzwɛ̃/
items.notes: The imparfait verb 'réveillait' and the noun 'réveil' share the same root but different endings that are easy to confuse.

items.fr: Les enfants adorent le sport collectif.
items.notes: The liaison between les and enfants turns into a clear z sound, so listen for lezenfants as one flowing unit.

items.fr: Je fais du sport chaque matin.
items.ipa: ʒə fɛ dy spɔʁ ʃak ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: The final t in sport is never pronounced, so do not add a sound after the silent letter.
Nous adorons is linked by a liaison z sound that makes the two words sound almost joined.
The verb ending -ent in gagnent is completely silent, so the word sounds just like gagne.

items.fr: Vous êtes doués pour le tennis.
items.notes: Vous êtes liaises with a z sound, linking the two words smoothly in speech.

items.fr: Le sport rend les enfants plus forts.
items.ipa: lə spɔʁ ʁɑ̃ le.zɑ̃.fɑ̃ ply fɔʁ
items.notes: The final d in rend is silent, so nothing is heard after the nasal vowel.

items.fr: Mon ami arrive au club à midi.
items.en: My friend arrives at the club at noon.
items.ipa: mɔ̃.na.mi a.ʁiv o klœb a mi.di
items.notes: Mon ami liaises with an n sound, so it sounds like monami rather than two separate words.

items.fr: Nous marchons longtemps dans les bois.
items.en: We walk for a long time in the woods.
items.ipa: nu maʁ.ʃɔ̃ lɔ̃.tɑ̃ dɑ̃ le bwa
items.notes: The final s in bois is silent, so the word ends on the vowel sound alone.

items.fr: Ils habitent près du grand stade.
items.en: They live near the big stadium.
items.notes: The h in habitent is silent but still allows a liaison, so ils habitent sounds like ilzabitent.

items.fr: Il fait un temps idéal pour jouer.
items.en: The weather is ideal for playing.
items.ipa: il fɛ œ̃ tɑ̃ i.de.al puʁ ʒwe
items.notes: Both the p and the s in temps stay silent, leaving only the nasal vowel sound.

items.fr: Elles arrivent tôt pour le match.
items.en: They arrive early for the match.
items.notes: Elles arrivent liaises with a z sound that glides the two words together.

items.fr: Elle porte des gants chauds pour le ski.
items.en: She wears warm gloves for skiing.
items.ipa: ɛl pɔʁt de ɡɑ̃ ʃo puʁ lə ski
items.notes: The final t and s in gants are both silent, so only the nasal vowel is heard.

items.fr: Un athlète entraîne les jeunes joueurs.
items.en: An athlete trains the young players.
items.notes: Un athlète liaises with an n sound because the silent h in athlète does not block it.

items.fr: Les enfants courent vite sur le terrain.
items.en: The children run fast on the field.
items.ipa: le.zɑ̃.fɑ̃ kuʁ vit syʁ lə tɛ.ʁɛ̃
items.notes: The ending -ent of courent is silent, so the verb is pronounced exactly like court.

items.en: These children love swimming a lot.
items.notes: Ces enfants is joined by a liaison z sound between the two words.

items.fr: Ils perdent rarement leurs matchs à domicile.
items.en: They rarely lose their home matches.
items.ipa: il pɛʁd ʁaʁ.mɑ̃ lœʁ matʃ a dɔ.mi.sil
items.notes: The -ent ending of perdent is silent, leaving the verb sounding like perd.

items.fr: Nos amis jouent au volley ce soir.
items.en: Our friends are playing volleyball tonight.
items.ipa: no.za.mi ʒu o vɔ.lɛ sə swaʁ
items.notes: Nos amis liaises with a z sound linking the plural possessive to the noun.

items.fr: Le corps a besoin de sport régulier.
items.ipa: lə kɔʁ a bə.zwɛ̃ də spɔʁ ʁe.ɡy.lje
items.notes: Both the p and the s at the end of corps stay silent.

items.fr: Deux athlètes attendent le début du match.
items.en: Two athletes are waiting for the start of the match.
items.ipa: dø.za.tlɛt a.tɑ̃d lə de.by dy matʃ
items.notes: Deux athlètes liaises with a z sound linking the number to the noun.

items.fr: Elle regarde souvent les matchs à la télé.
items.en: She often watches the matches on TV.
items.ipa: ɛl ʁə.ɡaʁd su.vɑ̃ le matʃ a la te.le
items.notes: The final t in souvent is silent, so only the nasal vowel is heard before the next word.

items.fr: Les élèves apprennent à nager cet été.
items.en: The students are learning to swim this summer.
items.notes: Les élèves liaises with a z sound joining the article to the noun.

items.fr: Nous jouons dans un grand champ derrière l'école.
items.en: We play in a big field behind the school.
items.ipa: nu ʒwɔ̃ dɑ̃.zœ̃ ɡʁɑ̃ ʃɑ̃ dɛ.ʁjɛʁ le.kɔl
items.notes: The final p in champ is completely silent, leaving only the nasal vowel sound.

items.fr: Son ami adore le football américain.
items.notes: Son ami liaises with an n sound linking the possessive to the vowel-initial noun.

items.fr: Ils adorent le sport depuis leur enfance.
items.en: They have loved sport since childhood.
items.notes: The -ent ending of adorent stays silent, so the verb sounds like adore.

items.fr: Vous allez au gymnase après l'école.
items.en: You go to the gym after school.
items.notes: Vous allez liaises with a z sound that connects the pronoun to the verb.

items.fr: Elle a mal au dos après le sport.
items.ipa: ɛl a mal o do a.pʁɛ lə spɔʁ
items.notes: The final s in dos is silent, so the word ends simply on the closed o sound.

items.fr: Trois enfants entrent dans la piscine.
items.en: Three children go into the pool.
items.notes: Trois enfants liaises with a z sound linking the number to the plural noun.

items.fr: Ce sport coûte cher pour les débutants.
items.en: This sport is expensive for beginners.
items.ipa: sə spɔʁ kut ʃɛʁ puʁ le de.by.tɑ̃
items.notes: The final t and s of débutants are both silent, leaving just the nasal vowel sound.

items.fr: Mes amis organisent un match amical.
items.en: My friends are organizing a friendly match.
items.notes: Mes amis liaises with a z sound between the possessive and the noun.

items.fr: Ils dansent tous les vendredis soirs.
items.ipa: il dɑ̃s tu le vɑ̃.dʁə.di swaʁ
items.notes: The -ent ending of dansent is silent, so the verb sounds identical to danse.

items.fr: Nous invitons un ancien joueur du club.
items.en: We are inviting a former player from the club.
items.notes: Nous invitons liaises with a z sound joining the subject pronoun to the verb.

items.fr: Elle porte toujours un legging gris pour courir.
items.en: She always wears grey leggings to run.
items.ipa: ɛl pɔʁt tu.ʒuʁ œ̃ le.ɡiŋ ɡʁi puʁ ku.ʁiʁ
items.notes: The final s in gris is silent, so the word ends on the vowel sound alone.

items.fr: Elle est allée à la piscine hier matin.
items.en: She went to the pool yesterday morning.
items.ipa: ɛl ɛ.ta.le a la pi.sin jɛʁ ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: Because aller takes être, the past participle allée adds a silent e to agree with the feminine subject elle.

items.fr: Il a couru à toute vitesse pendant le match.
items.en: He ran at full speed during the match.
items.ipa: il a ku.ʁy a tut vi.tɛs pɑ̃.dɑ̃ lə matʃ
items.notes: The verb form a and the preposition à sound identical, so only the accent distinguishes them in writing.

items.fr: Les joueurs ont gagné et on a organisé une fête.
items.en: The players won and we organized a party.
items.ipa: le ʒwœʁ ɔ̃ ɡa.ɲe e ɔ̃.na ɔʁ.ɡa.ni.ze yn fɛt
items.notes: Ont and on sound exactly the same, so listen to the sentence structure to know which spelling to write.

items.fr: Ils sont allés au club où ils s'entraînent le mardi.
items.en: They went to the club where they train on Tuesdays.
items.ipa: il sɔ̃.ta.le o klœb u il sɑ̃.tʁɛn lə maʁ.di
items.notes: Où meaning where is pronounced exactly like ou meaning or, so only context tells them apart.

items.fr: Le week-end, elle fait du sport ou elle se repose.
items.en: On weekends, she does sport or she rests.
items.ipa: lə wik.ɛnd ɛl fɛ dy spɔʁ u ɛl sə ʁə.poz
items.notes: Ou meaning or is a perfect homophone of où meaning where, so spelling depends purely on meaning.

items.fr: La joueuse que j'ai vue a marqué un but magnifique.
items.en: The player that I saw scored a magnificent goal.
items.ipa: la ʒwøz kə ʒe vy a maʁ.ke œ̃ by ma.ɲi.fik
items.notes: Because the direct object la joueuse comes before j'ai vue, the past participle vue must agree in the feminine.

items.fr: La salle de sport que nous avons visitée est très moderne.
items.en: The gym that we visited is very modern.
items.ipa: la sal də spɔʁ kə nu.za.vɔ̃ vi.zi.te ɛ tʁɛ mɔ.dɛʁn
items.notes: The preceding feminine object la salle forces the past participle visitée to take a silent extra e.

items.fr: On ira au stade si on a le temps demain.
items.en: We'll go to the stadium if we have time tomorrow.
items.ipa: ɔ̃.ni.ʁa o stad si ɔ̃.na lə tɑ̃ də.mɛ̃
items.notes: On a can sound like it could be written ont, so remember that on is always singular in form.

items.fr: Elle a fini son entraînement à huit heures.
items.en: She finished her training at eight o'clock.
items.ipa: ɛl a fi.ni sɔ̃.nɑ̃.tʁɛn.mɑ̃ a ɥi.tœʁ
items.notes: The verb a earlier in the sentence sounds just like the preposition à before huit heures.

items.fr: Mes sœurs sont arrivées en retard au tournoi.
items.en: My sisters arrived late to the tournament.
items.ipa: me sœʁ sɔ̃.ta.ʁi.ve ɑ̃ ʁə.taʁ o tuʁ.nwa
items.notes: Since sœurs is feminine plural, the être past participle arrivées must take both a silent e and s.

items.fr: Il a couru cinq kilomètres ou il a fait du vélo.
items.en: He ran five kilometers or he went cycling.
items.ipa: il a ku.ʁy sɛ̃k ki.lɔ.mɛtʁ u il a fɛ dy ve.lo
items.notes: Ou here means or and sounds identical to où meaning where, so context decides the spelling.

items.fr: Les filles que j'ai entraînées ont bien progressé.
items.en: The girls that I coached have progressed well.
items.ipa: le fij kə ʒe ɑ̃.tʁɛ.ne ɔ̃ bjɛ̃ pʁɔ.ɡʁɛ.se
items.notes: The preceding plural feminine object les filles makes entraînées agree with a silent es ending.

items.fr: Nous irons au club où on joue au badminton.
items.en: We will go to the club where we play badminton.
items.ipa: nu.zi.ʁɔ̃ o klœb u ɔ̃ ʒu o bad.min.tɔn
items.notes: Où indicating a place sounds exactly like ou meaning or, so only the accent marks the difference.

items.fr: On a perdu le match mais on va s'entraîner plus.
items.en: We lost the match but we are going to train more.
items.ipa: ɔ̃.na pɛʁ.dy lə matʃ mɛ ɔ̃ va sɑ̃.tʁɛ.ne ply
items.notes: On a is easy to confuse with ont by ear, even though on always stays singular.

items.fr: Les blessures qu'elle a eues étaient graves.
items.en: The injuries she had were serious.
items.ipa: le blɛ.syʁ kɛl a y e.tɛ ɡʁav
items.notes: The preceding feminine plural object les blessures makes the past participle eues agree with a silent es.

items.fr: Il ira au gymnase à sept heures ce soir.
items.en: He will go to the gym at seven o'clock tonight.
items.ipa: il i.ʁa o ʒim.naz a sɛ.tœʁ sə swaʁ
items.notes: The preposition à here must not be confused with the verb form a, even though they sound the same.

items.fr: Les médailles qu'ils ont gagnées sont dans le salon.
items.en: The medals that they won are in the living room.
items.ipa: le me.daj kil ɔ̃ ɡa.ɲe sɔ̃ dɑ̃ lə sa.lɔ̃
items.notes: The preceding feminine plural object les médailles forces gagnées to agree with a silent es ending.

items.fr: Il faut que tu fasses du sport régulièrement pour rester en forme.
items.en: You need to do sport regularly to stay fit.
items.ipa: il fo kə ty fas dy spɔʁ ʁe.ɡy.ljɛʁ.mɑ̃ puʁ ʁɛs.te ɑ̃ fɔʁm
items.notes: The subjunctive fasses comes from an irregular stem and does not resemble the indicative fais at all.

items.fr: Je doute qu'elle soit assez rapide pour gagner la course.
items.en: I doubt she is fast enough to win the race.
